name: Gonçalo Coelho
summary:
Gonçalo Coelho was a Portuguese explorer who belonged to a prominent family in northern Portugal. Born around 1470, he commanded two expeditions that explored much of the coast of Brazil between 1501 and 1512. These voyages significantly expanded Portuguese knowledge of the New World and established trade routes with the indigenous peoples of Brazil.

Coelho's achievements were crucial in shaping Portugal's colonial ambitions in South America during the early 16th century. His exploration of the Brazilian coast also laid the groundwork for subsequent European colonization efforts in the region.

The legacy of Gonçalo Coelho can be seen in the enduring impact of Portuguese culture and trade on Brazil, as well as the country's complex history of indigenous-European relations.

'In the 1512 expedition, we encountered a tribe that had never before seen Europeans. The encounter was peaceful, and we exchanged gifts and knowledge with them.' - Gonçalo Coelho's own account of his Brazilian voyages
